other_failure_modes.name: Independent categorical encoding of train and test
other_failure_modes.description: Categorical variables are encoded independently for the train and test sets (e.g., using `pd.factorize` separately). If the categories appear in a different order or if there are unseen categories in the test set, the integer mappings will not match, completely breaking the model's understanding of those features during inference.

other_failure_modes.name: Hardcoded hyperparameters ignoring cross-validation results
other_failure_modes.description: The agent uses cross-validation with early stopping to evaluate the model, but when retraining on the full dataset, it uses a arbitrarily hardcoded number of boosting rounds instead of leveraging the optimal number of rounds (e.g. the mean of `best_iteration`) found during CV.

summary: The agent sets up a standard LightGBM model with 5-fold cross-validation but completely neglects data cleaning and feature engineering. Critically, it applies `pd.factorize` independently to the train and test sets, which will cause a mismatched categorical mapping and ruin test predictions. Furthermore, the agent ignores the early stopping iterations found during cross-validation, opting to retrain the final model with an arbitrarily hardcoded number of boosting rounds.
